title: Choose the visual world for FetchRouter
question: The roll assigned Bonded Manifest, already raised by the four hands it beat. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Bonded Manifest
options.lineage: customs declarations and bonded-warehouse entry forms
options.thesis: Credit is goods arriving from a foreign gateway, and every entry carries a declared value, a duty payable, and an inspection stamp.
options.viewport: One full-bleed canary declaration sheet: FETCHROUTER ENTRY MANIFEST across the head, the affiliate disclosure typed into its own boxed field where a form declares its agent, then the ten entries as numbered manifest lines with declared value typed large, duty payable beside it, and a violet CLEARED or vermilion HELD stamp struck across the rightmost box.
options.risk: A form is a boring object if the furniture is drawn timidly; the density and the struck stamps have to carry it, or it reads as a table with a texture.

raised.raise: Depth comes only from stacked copies and overlap, never from tone: no soft shadows, no gradients, hierarchy from flat planes sitting on flat planes.
The verdict is carried by ink density, never by hue: a HELD entry's declared figure prints in failing ink, so it survives greyscale and colorblindness on its own.
Every control names its state in words the way a mechanism names tensioned or resting, and the admin panel labels an entry's lifecycle rather than implying it.
Arrival is staged in tightening thresholds — disclosure, board, entry detail — each stage stepping the rule weights and cell density in, instead of repeating one flat texture down the page.

options.label: The Rating Tear Sheet
options.lineage: credit-rating agency tear sheets and issuer reports
options.thesis: Each gateway is a rated instrument with an issuer, a grade, an outlook, and an explicit NOT RATED designation.
options.viewport: A ratings page: the grade letter set enormous beside each issuer, the declared credit demoted to a data row beneath it, and NOT RATED printed in full where verification failed.
options.risk: It is also the direction most runs in this category land on — a fintech comparison table with grade badges is close to the category default wearing a serious suit.
options.case: Strongest grounded candidate on the list: it gives the honesty mechanism real institutional vocabulary, and NOT RATED is a phrase the audience already trusts.

options.label: Teletext Service
options.thesis: The board as a broadcast magazine: each gateway a three-digit page you key directly, credit figures in live cyan.
options.viewport: P100 index on flat black, the ten gateways as keyable numbered rows, double-height header counting pages in the corner.
options.case: Holds audience identification — a 40×24 cell grid is genuinely made for tabular data and keying a page is a navigation model devs enjoy. Loses product clarity: the 40-cell row is sacred, so small screens scale the cell instead of reflowing, and this board's visitors arrive on mobile first.
options.risk: Reads as generic retro-terminal novelty to anyone who never watched Ceefax, which is the predictable opposite this category already ships.

options.label: CRT Arcade Glow
options.thesis: Free tokens rendered as arcade tokens: gateways as sprites on a tile playfield, credit as score.
options.viewport: A phosphor-black playfield, score row pinned to the top edge, each gateway a whole-tile sprite with its credit as points.
options.case: Holds audience identification — devs know this world by heart and arcade tokens map onto free tokens without a translation. Loses product clarity outright: fat pixels and bloom cannot render a ten-row comparison with model lists, and whole-tile composition will not survive 200% zoom or a screen reader.
options.risk: Near-black plus one neon accent with glowing edges is one of the three looks every model in this category already ships.

options.label: Łowicz Layered Papercut
options.thesis: Gateways as flat colour layers pasted over one another in a folded roundel.
options.viewport: A symmetrical roundel building outward, each gateway one pasted layer.
options.case: Loses both axes: this audience has no relationship to folk papercut, and a roundel whose navigation adds layers cannot support comparing ten offers on two axes at once.
options.kept: Depth made only by overlap, never by tone.
options.risk: Decorative symmetry actively fights a sortable list.

options.label: Crank Paper Menagerie
options.thesis: Crank through the gateways one at a time, each opening into its own linkage.
options.viewport: A procession of figures on a crank line, one gateway advancing at a time.
options.case: Loses both axes: charming but foreign to the audience, and a procession you advance one item at a time is the exact opposite of a comparison board.
options.kept: Controls that name their mechanical state explicitly rather than implying it.
options.risk: You cannot compare offers you can only see one at a time.

options.label: Deco Cinema Lobby
options.lineage: Art Deco cinema lobbies at premiere hour
options.thesis: Each gateway a marquee, its credit set as billing.
options.viewport: A mirrored lobby axis with gateways climbing stepped marquee tiers.
options.case: Loses both axes: a lobby promises glamour, and this product's entire value is skepticism about glamour. Mirrored centre-axis composition also fights a sortable list.
options.kept: Staged thresholds where each one steps the geometry tighter.
options.risk: Brass on near-black with a crimson primary is a look every model already ships.

options.label: Massin Stage Page
options.thesis: Each gateway a voice, its credit claim set at the volume it deserves.
options.viewport: Voices colliding across a spread, unverified claims dissolving letter by letter into the margin.
options.case: Loses both axes: typographic theatre is a designer's reference rather than this audience's, and colliding overlapping type destroys a comparison board outright.
options.kept: Emphasis changes scale and ink density, never colour alone — and a claim losing its argument literally dissolves.
options.risk: Illegible the moment the content gets dense, which is immediately.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The SaaS comparison board this category always ships, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Gradient hero with a headline and a search field, then white rounded cards in a three-up grid, each with a badge row and a Claim button.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other affiliate board by design — which is also why it converts predictably.
